extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII.

Annex VII (notified body) assessment is mandatory for high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (e.g. biometric identification systems) unless harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied, in which case internal control (Annex VI) may be used for some; for most other Annex III high-risk systems, internal control (Annex VI) is sufficient.

For high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products covered by Section A of Annex I (existing EU product legislation, e.g. machinery, medical devices), providers must follow the conformity assessment procedure required under that existing legislation, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements.

A provider may choose any notified body for the conformity assessment under Annex VII, except that where a high-risk AI system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, the relevant market surveillance authority under Article 74(8) or (9) acts as the notified body.
Substantial modifications to a high-risk AI system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority, by way of derogation from Article 43 and upon a duly justified request, to authorise placing on the market or putting into service of a specific high-risk AI system for exceptional reasons (public security, protection of life and health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets), for a limited period.

Under Annex VII, where necessary and after all other reasonable means have been exhausted, a notified body may, upon reasoned request, be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, subject to existing EU law on intellectual property and trade secrets.
Article 43(5) of the AI Act gives the European Commission power to adopt delegated acts to update Annex VI and Annex VII in light of technical progress, without needing to revise the Act itself.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes requirements for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies.

A Council document (7322/26) describes a coding system (e.g., AIP 0101–0105) used to define the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under Article 30 for AI systems subject to Annex I.

A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836 / 2025/0359 (COD)) proposes creating a new Annex XIV listing codes and corresponding types of AI systems for the NANDO notified-body information system, and proposes amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements into aviation safety regulation.

As of March 2026, no AI Act-specific notified bodies had yet been designated; the designation process across member states was still ongoing, with limited capacity and uncertain timelines ahead of the August 2026 deadline.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical device AI systems (MDR/IVDR interplay context).
As of late June 2026, zero notified bodies had been designated under the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) in the NANDO database, a separate but related regulatory regime also relying on notified bodies.

One source states that post-2026, notified bodies designated under the AI Act will begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, with overlap to existing MDR/IVDR notified body assessments.
As of October 2025, the NANDO system listed 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies (for medical devices, not AI Act-specific).
The Commission publishes a list of designated notified bodies in the NANDO information system, filterable by legislation.

One news source claims that under a 'final text agreed in September 2026,' the start date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations was moved to 2 August 2029 (from a previously reported 2 December 2027), citing lack of readiness of harmonised standards and notified bodies.
Other sources state the August 2026 deadline for high-risk AI obligations (including conformity assessment, CE marking, and registration) remains applicable and 'isn't moving.'

A 2022 proposal version of Article 43 (pre-adoption text, 25 November 2022) set out conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems in Annex III point 1 involving harmonised standards or common specifications, as part of the legislative proposal stage before the Act's final adoption.

contradictions.claim_b: Multiple other sources from 2026 continue to reference an August 2026 deadline as the operative date for high-risk AI obligations, with no mention of a shift to 2029.

This conflicts with sources 21, 23, and 28, which treat August 2026 as the binding, non-moving deadline for high-risk AI Act compliance. No official EU source in this set confirms the 2029 change, making source 15's claim unverified against official adopted text.

contradictions.claim_b: Source 23 implies notified-body AI Act assessments would begin only 'post-2026,' consistent with no designations yet, but frames August 2026 as when 'high-risk AI obligations fully apply' without acknowledging any gap caused by absent notified bodies.
contradictions.description: There is tension between sources indicating the August 2026 deadline is firm and fully binding (source 23) and sources indicating that notified bodies — required for certain high-risk conformity assessments — are not yet designated as of March/April 2026, raising questions about how the deadline can be met for systems requiring notified body involvement (sources 21, 22).

open_issues: No source in this set confirms whether any notified bodies have actually been designated under the AI Act (Article 29/30 designation) as of October 2026; the most recent explicit statements (March/April 2026) say zero have been designated, but no update closer to the current date (October 2026) is provided.

It is unclear from the sources whether the Commission's proposed new Annex XIV and NANDO coding system (sources 8, 9) have been formally adopted as law or remain at proposal stage, and when any such regulation would enter into force.
The relationship between the conflicting Article 46 derogation procedure and standard Article 43 timelines is not fully detailed, e.g., what 'limited period' means in practice.

Sources do not clarify whether the 2 August 2029 date (source 15) is an officially adopted amendment to the AI Act's timeline or a misreported/unconfirmed claim, since no official EUR-Lex or Council text in the provided sources corroborates it.
It is unclear which specific organizations (companies) have applied for or received notified body status specifically under the AI Act, as opposed to under MDR/IVDR or CRA frameworks.

The sources do not specify how conformity assessment procedures interact with the Article 97 delegated act process for updating Annexes VI and VII, e.g., whether any such delegated acts have been adopted.

It is not clear from the sources how AI Act notified body designations (Article 29/30) will interact with existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies in practice, e.g., whether the same organizations will hold dual designations or separate bodies will be created.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures and Notified Body Designation Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems, combining internal control with mandatory third-party (notified body) review for certain categories, most notably biometric identification systems ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). However, the practical infrastructure to support this system—designated notified bodies—appears largely absent as of early-to-mid 2026, creating significant uncertainty about how compliance deadlines can be met ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [MDxCRO](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 establishes two primary conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or third-party assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)). Annex VII notified-body assessment is mandatory for high-risk systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (e.g., biometric identification), unless harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied, in which case internal control may suffice; for most other Annex III systems, internal control alone is generally sufficient (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

For high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products already covered by EU product legislation (Annex I, Section A—e.g., machinery, medical devices), providers must follow the existing sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)).

Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions—in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body under Article 74(8)/(9) (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications generally trigger a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from Article 43 for a limited period on exceptional grounds such as public security or health protection (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Under Annex VII, notified bodies may, as a last resort, be granted reasoned access to training and trained models, subject to IP and trade secret protections (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Despite the legal framework, no source confirms actual designation of AI Act-specific notified bodies. As of March 2026, no such bodies had been designated, with the process still ongoing across member states ahead of the August 2026 deadline (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). Similarly, as of April 2026, none had been formally designated for medical-device AI systems under MDR/IVDR overlap (low confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). A related regime, the Cyber Resilience Act, reportedly had zero designated notified bodies in NANDO as of late June 2026 (low confidence) ([CyberCertLabs](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026)). For context, by October 2025 NANDO listed 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies—unrelated to AI Act designation specifically (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Regulatory groundwork continues: a Council document references a coding system (AIP 0101–0105) for defining notified-body designation scope (medium confidence) ([Council Document 7322/26](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)), and a Commission proposal would create a new Annex XIV for NANDO codes and integrate AI Act requirements into aviation safety regulation (medium confidence) ([COM(2025) 836](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A low-confidence news blog claims the Annex III high-risk deadline was pushed to 2 August 2029 under a "September 2026 final text" ([AI Act News Blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)), contradicting multiple sources asserting the August 2026 deadline remains firm ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)). No official EU source corroborates the 2029 date. There is also tension between the firm August 2026 deadline and reports of zero designated notified bodies as of March/April 2026, raising feasibility questions. The delegated-act power under Article 43(5) to update Annexes VI/VII is cited at low confidence with no evidence of actual use ([FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unconfirmed whether any notified bodies have been designated as of October 2026. The adoption status of the proposed Annex XIV/NANDO coding system is unclear. Details on Article 46's "limited period" derogations are sparse. The accuracy of the 2029 deadline claim is unverified. No sources identify specific organizations seeking AI Act notified body status, nor clarify interaction with existing MDR/IVDR bodies.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures and Notified Body Designation Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems, combining internal control with mandatory third-party (notified body) review for certain categories, most notably biometric identification systems ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). However, the practical infrastructure to support this system—designated notified bodies—appears largely absent as of early-to-mid 2026, creating significant uncertainty about how compliance deadlines can be met ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [MDxCRO](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 establishes two primary conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or third-party assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)). Annex VII notified-body assessment is mandatory for high-risk systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (e.g., biometric identification), unless harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied, in which case internal control may suffice; for most other Annex III systems, internal control alone is generally sufficient (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

For high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products already covered by EU product legislation (Annex I, Section A—e.g., machinery, medical devices), providers must follow the existing sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)).

Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions—in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body under Article 74(8)/(9) (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications generally trigger a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from Article 43 for a limited period on exceptional grounds such as public security or health protection (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Under Annex VII, notified bodies may, as a last resort, be granted reasoned access to training and trained models, subject to IP and trade secret protections (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Despite the legal framework, no source confirms actual designation of AI Act-specific notified bodies. As of March 2026, no such bodies had been designated, with the process still ongoing across member states ahead of the August 2026 deadline (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). Similarly, as of April 2026, none had been formally designated for medical-device AI systems under MDR/IVDR overlap (low confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). A related regime, the Cyber Resilience Act, reportedly had zero designated notified bodies in NANDO as of late June 2026 (low confidence) ([CyberCertLabs](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026)). For context, by October 2025 NANDO listed 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies—unrelated to AI Act designation specifically (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Regulatory groundwork continues: a Council document references a coding system (AIP 0101–0105) for defining notified-body designation scope (medium confidence) ([Council Document 7322/26](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)), and a Commission proposal would create a new Annex XIV for NANDO codes and integrate AI Act requirements into aviation safety regulation (medium confidence) ([COM(2025) 836](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A low-confidence news blog claims the Annex III high-risk deadline was pushed to 2 August 2029 under a "September 2026 final text" ([AI Act News Blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)), contradicting multiple sources asserting the August 2026 deadline remains firm ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)). No official EU source corroborates the 2029 date. There is also tension between the firm August 2026 deadline and reports of zero designated notified bodies as of March/April 2026, raising feasibility questions. The delegated-act power under Article 43(5) to update Annexes VI/VII is cited at low confidence with no evidence of actual use ([FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unconfirmed whether any notified bodies have been designated as of October 2026. The adoption status of the proposed Annex XIV/NANDO coding system is unclear. Details on Article 46's "limited period" derogations are sparse. The accuracy of the 2029 deadline claim is unverified. No sources identify specific organizations seeking AI Act notified body status, nor clarify interaction with existing MDR/IVDR bodies.
